abstract: Protein modeling has largely centered on sequence representations, leaving the geometry and physicochemical context of molecular surfaces underused. We introduce PSMa (Protein Surface Masked autoencoder), a self-supervised framework that operates directly on molecular-surface point clouds with geometric and physicochemical attributes, reconstructing masked surface patches to learn transferable representations at scale from ∼220,000 PDB structures. On held-out proteins, PSMa outperforms sequence-only and structure-only baselines on two downstream tasks─(i) protein-protein interface (PPI) binding-site identification and (ii) protein thermal-stability prediction─matching state-of-the-art AUROC and AUPRC while substantially improving threshold-dependent classification performance. The learned representations generalize across protein-length ranges and across experimental as well as predicted structures, with decision thresholds closer to the neutral prior; these findings show that surface-centric pretraining provides a strong, generalizable foundation for structure-aware protein machine learning.
